name: Can a detached ADU be rented separately in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Can a detached ADU in Los Angeles be used as a separate long-term rental, and what design choices make it more marketable?
mainEntity.text: Can a detached ADU in Los Angeles be used as a separate long-term rental, and what design choices make it more marketable?

acceptedAnswer.text: A detached ADU is often most valuable when it functions like a true standalone home. Separate rental appeal usually comes from privacy, a dedicated entrance, efficient layout, natural light, and finishes that feel durable rather than temporary. In-unit laundry, a real kitchen, and thoughtful storage can make a big difference in renter interest. From a construction standpoint, sound control and privacy matter just as much as square footage. Homeowners should also think about outdoor space, mailbox or address setup, and lighting around the entry. The more the unit feels like an independent residence, the stronger the rental positioning. When planning for rental use, the design should avoid awkward circulation, dead corners, and undersized living areas. Even if the unit is not rented immediately, building for long-term usability usually improves resale appeal and flexibility later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Detached ADUs are commonly used as separate long-term rentals when local rules allow. Marketability improves with a private entrance, strong sound separation, good storage, in-unit laundry, and a layout that feels independent from the main house.
